newsitem.title: USA: Mass. Gov says no plans to sell pension bonds.
newsitem.headline: Mass. Gov says no plans to sell pension bonds.

text.p: Massachusetts Gov. William Weld said Friday the state is not currently considering the sale of pension bonds.
Weld, speaking at a conference on the campus of North Carolina State University, was responding to a question after his presentation about pension bonds and paying off an unfunded liability.
"We are retiring that pretty quickly on a pay-as-you-go basis," Weld said. "We think we are moving in the right direction. I don't think we need to" sell pension bonds.
Weld was attending an "Emerging Issues Forum," which focuses on economic policies for the future. He spoke on states competing in the global marketplace.

A number of states are currently considering pension bond sales to pay for their unfunded liabilities. New Jersey and Michigan are mulling sales of about $3 billion each. Iowa is also studying the possibility of a pension bond sale.
